about.label: Get to know
about.heading: What is the Chiang Rai Night Bazaar?
about.lead: The Chiang Rai Night Bazaar is the city's best-known evening market, on Phahon Yothin Road close to the Golden Clock Tower and the Old City gate.
about.paragraph1: After dark the street fills with stalls selling handicrafts, textiles, jewellery, souvenirs and hill-tribe goods from the Akha, Karen, Lisu, Lahu and Hmong communities. There are also restaurants, Thai massage and street performances.
about.paragraph2: It is also a great starting point for nearby sights such as Wat Phra Kaew, the King Mengrai Monument and the Mae Kok River, making the market both a shopping spot and the heart of Chiang Rai's night culture.
about.quote: Come after dark — that's when the whole street lights up with stalls, food smoke and music.

history.label: History & lore
history.heading: The story of Chiang Rai's night market
history.intro: The market grew alongside Chiang Rai's rise as a tourist base in the 1990s, when travellers began using the city as a stopover for the Golden Triangle — yet the area's historical and Lanna cultural roots run far deeper.

blocks.title: Lanna heritage
blocks.text: Chiang Rai was once the capital of the Lanna Kingdom and a long-standing caravan crossroads, so handicrafts, textiles, silver and hill-tribe goods have accumulated here for generations — the very soul of this night market.

blocks.title: The Golden Clock Tower
blocks.text: A short walk from the market stands the Golden Art Clock Tower (Chiang Rai Clock Tower), designed and built in 2008 by Chalermchai Kositpipat — the artist behind Chiang Rai's famous White Temple (Wat Rong Khun). Its golden crown glows as the city's favourite meeting point and a symbol of modern Chiang Rai. It is often wrongly attributed to Thawan Duchanee, creator of the Black House Museum (Baandam Museum) — that artist is unrelated to this clock tower.

blocks.title: A night-time cultural hub
blocks.text: Today the market blends commerce, food and performance, expressing a modern Chiang Rai identity that still keeps its Lanna cultural roots.

blocks.title: Nearby historical landmarks
blocks.text: A short walk away is Wat Phra Kaew, the original home of the Emerald Buddha — Thailand's most revered image — alongside the King Mengrai Monument and the Mae Kok River, all anchoring the area's deep history.

legend.title: Local legend
legend.text: The striking Golden Clock Tower, a short walk from the market, was designed in 2008 by Chalermchai Kositpipat, the artist behind Chiang Rai's White Temple. Locals say its golden crown honours the glory of old Lanna, and it has become the meeting point everyone trusts.

didYouKnow.title: Did you know?
didYouKnow.text: Chiang Rai Night Bazaar opens daily beside the Old Bus Terminal; if you visit on a Saturday or Sunday, you can also stroll the city's separate weekend walking streets — the Saturday Walking Street (Thanalai Road) and the Sunday Walking Street. These are different locations and run by different organisers from the night bazaar, so don't confuse them.

scamTip.text: Cheap 'designer' goods are usually fakes — bargain to about half the asking price. For food, check the price on the sign before ordering.

food.label: Must-try eats
food.heading: Food at the Chiang Rai Night Bazaar
food.lead: The market mixes restaurants, a food court and roadside stalls, covering Northern Thai and street food in one place.

dishes.name: Khao soi
dishes.desc: Curry-noodle soup, a Northern Thailand classic

dishes.name: Sai ua
dishes.desc: Northern herb sausage with chili dip

dishes.name: Khanom Jeen Nam Ngiew
dishes.desc: Chiang Rai's most iconic local noodle soup — a red broth of dried cotton-tree flower and pork blood, sour and aromatic

dishes.name: Jim Jum (clay-pot hotpot)
dishes.desc: The signature scene of the food court — slow-cooked in a clay pot; many visitors come just to eat hotpot while watching the show

dishes.name: Mango sticky rice
dishes.desc: A crowd-favourite sweet of ripe mango and warm sticky rice

quote.text: Shop till you're hungry, then grab a roadside plate — the smell of khao soi is the signal you've arrived in Chiang Rai.
quote.author: A local food blogger

cultureShow.label: Cultural shows
cultureShow.heading: Free shows at the night market
cultureShow.lead: What sets Chiang Rai Night Bazaar apart from many others is its free traditional performances every night — the part locals are most proud of.
cultureShow.tip: Head to the central stage area around 19:30–20:30 to catch free Lanna dance and traditional instrument performances.

stages.title: Cultural Stage
stages.desc: Deep inside the market, free Lanna traditional dance and classical music — the most ceremonial performance space.

stages.title: Food Court Stage
stages.desc: Accompanied by folk singing or contemporary acts; eat while you watch in a relaxed, lively atmosphere.

nearby.label: 10-minute walking loop
nearby.heading: Worth a stroll nearby
nearby.lead: All within walking distance of the market, these two landmarks fit perfectly into an evening route.

items.title: Clock Tower light show
items.desc: Lights up at 19:00 / 20:00 / 21:00 nightly, about a 10-minute walk — the best photo spot before or after the market.

items.title: King Mengrai Monument
items.desc: Honouring King Mengrai, founder of Chiang Rai, about a 10-minute walk — a local landmark that explains the city's origins.

tips.label: Culture & payment tips
tips.heading: A few reminders before you go
tips.lead: A few practical tips to make the experience smoother and more respectful of locals.

items.title: Cash first
items.desc: Most stalls are cash-only (Thai baht); the food court also usually asks you to order and pay first — carry small change.

items.title: Order at the food court first
items.desc: At the food court you usually order and pay at the stall before sitting down — watch each stall's pickup flow.

items.title: Bargain politely
items.desc: Respect hill-tribe craft makers; keep bargaining friendly — admire first, then negotiate.

markets.label: Market guide
markets.heading: Chiang Rai's three night markets — don't mix them up
markets.lead: Many visitors confuse the daily Night Bazaar with the Saturday and Sunday walking streets. They run in different locations, on different days. This guide covers the nightly Chiang Rai Night Bazaar.

rows.name: Chiang Rai Night Bazaar (this guide)
rows.location: Phahon Yothin Rd, next to Bus Terminal 1
rows.features: Permanent stalls & food courts, free shows on two stages, mostly under cover in rain

rows.name: Saturday Walking Street
rows.features: Handicrafts & street food, one day only

markets.note: The walking streets are within easy reach of the Night Bazaar — on weekends you can do both. Times can change, so check locally on the day.

activity.slippery: Paths may be slippery — wear shoes with good grip.
activity.niceEvening: Lovely weather: a great evening for the market and a free Lanna dance show.

Wind down: last souvenirs, or an affordable foot massage

services.label: Visitor services & facilities
services.heading: Restrooms, parking, food — the practical rundown
services.lead: A neutral, type-level overview of nearby facilities to help you plan ahead; conditions on the ground may vary.
services.neutralNote: This is a non-profit educational guide: we recommend no specific businesses and stay strictly neutral. Facilities may change — please rely on what you find on site.

items.title: Restrooms (WC)
items.desc: Public restrooms serve the market area, some with a small fee (around 5–10 THB); nearby malls and hotel lobbies often have restrooms for visitors too.

items.title: Parking
items.desc: Expect street-side spaces and paid public lots nearby; spots get tight at dusk, so arrive early or come by songthaew or on foot.

items.title: Food & drink
items.desc: The market brings together snack stalls, Northern Thai restaurants and a food court, including vegetarian options; convenience stores and local eateries sit nearby.

items.title: Lodging
items.desc: Budget guesthouses, hostels and boutique hotels are all within walking distance; book ahead in high season.

items.title: Shops & convenience
items.desc: 24-hour convenience stores dot the surroundings, with supermarkets for water, snacks and daily necessities.

items.title: Fuel & charging
items.desc: Petrol stations line the main roads; EV charging points are growing across the city — plan refuelling ahead if driving or renting an EV.

items.title: Money & payment
items.desc: ATMs and currency-exchange counters are easy to find; most stalls are cash-first, some take local mobile payment — keep some Thai baht handy.

items.title: Getting around
items.desc: Red songthaews are the main local transport, hop-on hop-off; ride-hailing apps work too, and booking early helps at the late-night rush.

items.title: Health & pharmacy
items.desc: Pharmacies nearby stock common medicines, mosquito repellent and sunscreen; hospitals and clinics are available in the city centre.

stewardship.label: Culture & responsibility
stewardship.heading: Be a welcome visitor
stewardship.lead: The market is local people's livelihood and a shop window for Lanna culture. A little background knowledge and courtesy go a long way.
stewardship.eduTitle: Understanding: the culture behind the market

edu.title: From caravan route to tourist landmark
edu.text: Founded in 1262, Chiang Rai was the Lanna Kingdom's first capital and a caravan crossroads between Yunnan, Burma and Siam — its market tradition is centuries old. Since the 1990s it has grown into the tourist landmark you see today.

edu.title: A showcase of hill-tribe crafts
edu.text: Textiles, silverwork and embroidery by the Akha, Karen, Lisu, Lahu and Hmong communities are the market's most meaningful goods — every handmade piece carries generations of skill.

edu.title: "Meet you under the Clock Tower"
edu.text: The Golden Clock Tower was designed by Chalermchai Kositpipat, artist of the White Temple. Its glowing crown is now the city's default meeting point, anchoring countless "meet you under the Clock Tower" promises.

responsibilities.title: Reduce waste
responsibilities.text: Bring your own bag and bottle, and use the designated bins to help keep the street clean.

responsibilities.title: Respect makers & vendors
responsibilities.text: Crafts embody generations of hill-tribe skill — bargain kindly, and always ask before photographing people or their goods.

responsibilities.title: Dress & behave considerately
responsibilities.text: Thailand values politeness: cover shoulders and knees at nearby temples, and keep noise down during performances.

responsibilities.title: Shop sensibly
responsibilities.text: Be wary of 'designer' goods at implausibly low prices; wildlife products such as ivory are illegal — never buy them.

responsibilities.title: Care for animals & nature
responsibilities.text: Skip rides, feeding and other animal-entertainment activities, and choose responsible ways to travel.
